# Required status-check contexts for master, one per line.
#
# This is the authoritative committed list. The required-checks-drift job in
# .circleci/continue_config.yml compares it against the LIVE configuration on
# every push and reports both directions of drift: a context that is committed
# here but not required on master is a gate that does not block a merge, and a
# context required on master that no job emits is fail-closed and blocks every
# merge forever.
#
# WHERE THE LIVE CONFIGURATION LIVES: classic branch protection on master
# (/repos/arangodb/kube-arangodb/branches/master/protection), not a repository
# ruleset. The only rules that reach this branch through the ruleset API are the
# two enterprise-sourced ones, deletion and non_fast_forward, and neither can
# carry status checks. Classic protection on master also requires signed commits
# and one approving code-owner review.
#
# HOW THESE STRINGS ARE OBTAINED: read off a real pipeline with
# `gh pr checks <n> --repo arangodb/kube-arangodb`, never hand-derived. CircleCI
# appends an instance suffix (`-1`, `-2`) to the context of a job it considers
# duplicated across the config, and the numbering is not predictable from the
# config text. Every workflow entry in continue_config.yml therefore carries an
# explicit unique name, and check-code deliberately appears in one workflow only,
# which is what keeps the one string already required below stable.

# --- Required on master today (verified against the live protection) ----------
ci/circleci: check-code

# --- Blocking gates added by the security suite ------------------------------
# disposition-check is the integrity control over the exception path: an undated
# or expired suppression, or a SAST scope reduction, must not be mergeable.
ci/circleci: disposition-check
# Diff-aware SAST at WARNING over new code only. The full-repo tier is
# report-only while its 9 pre-existing ERROR findings are open, so this is the
# tier that holds new code to a band.
ci/circleci: sast-scan-diff
# The job carries the deterministic Dockerfile credential guard, which fails the
# build on a build-time credential surviving into a final stage. The
# misconfiguration scan inside the same job is report-only.
ci/circleci: misconfig-scan

# --- Deliberately NOT required yet, each with its flip criterion -------------
# ci/circleci: dependency-cve-scan   warn-only by team decision (#2118). One
#     fixable HIGH is open at this commit (CVE-2026-56852, golang.org/x/text)
#     and the companion dependency-bump PR clears it. Add this line in the same
#     change that sets fail-on-findings: true.
# ci/circleci: image-cve-scan        warn-only by team decision (#2132). The
#     released 1.4.4 image carries five fixable HIGH findings in the compiled
#     operator binary, four of them already fixed on master, so this can only go
#     blocking after a release ships the fixes.
# ci/circleci: image-cve-scan-ubi    same, and the UBI9 base adds seven more
#     fixable HIGH findings in its own package set.
# ci/circleci: secret-scan           report-only until the nine private-key
#     findings in the two agency-state fixtures under
#     pkg/deployment/agency/state/testdata/ are redacted or given a dated,
#     owner-approved acceptance. See .circleci/trivy-secret.yaml.
# ci/circleci: sast-scan             report-only until the nine ERROR findings
#     listed in SECURITY.md are cleared or dispositioned by their owners.
# ci/circleci: vulncheck             the repository's own govulncheck, which
#     predates this rollout and now has its own job, context and nightly run.
#     Still on the Makefile's -optional target: `make vulncheck` exits 3 with
#     five reachable findings and only GO-2026-5970 (x/text) is fixable in
#     range. Flipping to `make vulncheck` and adding this line is Adam's call,
#     and needs the executor image on 1.25.12+ plus a decision on containerd v1
#     and x/crypto/openpgp.
# ci/circleci: required-checks-drift the drift job itself is warn-only while
#     this list is incomplete; making it required is the last step, after the
#     lines above are all in place on both sides.
#
# ADDING A LINE HERE DOES NOT CONFIGURE ANYTHING. Branch protection is edited by
# a repository admin; this file is the record the drift job checks it against.
